thesis: Today's -8.9% single-day drop tracks broader profit-taking across AI-data-center infrastructure names and lingering caution from Vertiv's July 29 Q2 revenue miss, not a fresh company-specific disclosure; sell-side sentiment stays broadly bullish (24 of 28 analysts at Buy/Strong Buy) and one analyst has floated substantial further upside. Multiple law firms (Pomerantz, Schall Brown & Schwartz, Hagens Berman) opened investor-loss investigations in August tied to the July guidance miss, but none has produced a confirmed finding or scheduled hearing date. Because today's move reads as sector-wide/technical rather than a new deterioration in the underlying AI power-infrastructure demand story, this still supports holding, though the unresolved investigations and sensitivity to any further guidance disappointment keep conviction low.
invalidation: A confirmed adverse finding or scheduled hearing date in the securities-fraud investigations, or a fresh company-specific guidance cut/order cancellation, rather than continued sector-wide AI-infrastructure profit-taking.

thesis: SK hynix posted record Q2 2026 revenue and operating income on AI-driven HBM demand and began HBM4 mass-production shipments, with a broader ramp planned for H2 2026, yet shares initially fell nearly 9% on the print as results still missed the Street's elevated estimates; the stock has since rallied back to within 0.6% of its 52-week high as the HBM4 ramp narrative reasserted itself. A DRAM price-fixing class action (filed June 25, 2026, alongside Samsung and Micron) and a long-running Chinese SAMR antitrust probe are real overhangs, but neither has a scheduled ruling or hearing date, so they don't yet threaten the near-term operating picture. Because the market's own reaction to the print was mixed rather than uniformly confirming, this stays medium rather than high conviction.
invalidation: A scheduled ruling/hearing date being set in the DRAM price-fixing case, a confirmed guidance cut on HBM4 ramp timing, or a Q3 shipment miss.

thesis: AXT reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $47.6M (vs. $34.1M est.) and EPS of $0.19 (vs. $0.07 est.), driven by record indium phosphide substrate demand for AI data-center optical links, with backlog now above $100M; Needham, Wedbush and Northland all raised price targets on the print. A 2021-2024-period securities class action and an April 2024 short-seller report alleging overstated property holdings and environmental violations remain open, but neither has produced a confirmed finding or a scheduled hearing date, and AXT's April 2026 $550M equity raise (more than 90 days ago, funding indium phosphide capacity expansion) is already priced in rather than a fresh dilution event. The demand and margin inflection is company-specific and already realized in the print, not a forecast.
invalidation: Confirmed findings or a scheduled hearing date in the pending securities litigation, or a reversal in indium phosphide backlog/bookings.

thesis: Dell posted record fiscal Q2 revenue of $47B (+58% YoY) and EPS of $6.34 (+273% YoY), booked a record $60.9B in AI-server orders, exited the quarter with a $95B backlog, and raised full-year guidance to 69% sales growth; shares gained as much as 10% on the print. An ERISA suit over 401(k) plan fund performance is pending but unrelated to core operations and carries no scheduled hearing date. Shares are already up 236% year-to-date, which raises valuation risk, but the record backlog and raised guidance indicate durable order demand rather than sentiment alone driving the move.
invalidation: AI-server order cancellations, backlog erosion, or a guidance cut in a future quarter.

thesis: CoreWeave's Q2 2026 revenue more than doubled YoY to $2.58B, beating estimates, with backlog swelling to roughly $104B and full-year guidance raised; shares rallied 18-20% on the print, Truist lifted its price target, and Nvidia increased its equity stake in the company. A securities class action covering the March-December 2025 period is pending (lead-plaintiff deadline already passed in March 2026) with no scheduled hearing date, and while heavy capex and widening losses are real concerns some analysts have flagged for new investors, the roughly $104B backlog and Nvidia's expanded stake indicate committed demand and capital-partner support behind the growth, not just sentiment.
invalidation: Backlog cancellations, a customer-concentration shock, or a scheduled ruling/hearing date emerging in the pending securities litigation.

thesis: Nvidia is trading near its all-time high after formally announcing a $12.9B acquisition of Hugging Face to scale LLM/open-source model support, with an appearance at the Goldman Sachs conference on September 10 still ahead — a pending, not-yet-realized catalyst that keeps this capped below high conviction. China's SAMR has found Nvidia in violation of anti-monopoly terms tied to the 2020 Mellanox approval and is continuing its investigation, but no penalty or scheduled ruling date has been announced. The 60-day price move only marginally clears the signal threshold, and the read here leans more on continued AI-infrastructure demand momentum than any single already-realized catalyst.
invalidation: A confirmed penalty or scheduled ruling from the China antitrust proceeding, or a materially negative Goldman Sachs conference update.

thesis: XP's Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.67 beat the $2.59 estimate on revenue of $4.88B, with client assets rising to BRL2.2T and net new money of BRL28B, yet shares slipped roughly 2% combined in regular and after-hours trading as investors stayed cautious on revenue mix and near-term outlook. A 2024 short-seller report alleging a 'Madoff-like' scheme tied to a subsidiary product remains under investigation by multiple law firms with no confirmed finding or scheduled hearing date. The beat is real and company-specific, but the market's own tepid reaction and the unresolved fraud allegation leave the read mixed rather than clearly resolved.
invalidation: A confirmed finding from the fraud-allegation investigation, or continued declines in net new money/client assets.

thesis: SPCX is a Robinhood-issued tokenized debt security tracking SpaceX (now merged with xAI/Grok), not a direct equity claim, and today's price sits below its level from 60 days ago on an intraday basis despite a nominal +10.3% 60-day close-to-close move, coinciding with the first of several scheduled token lock-up expirations running from today through December 8, 2026 — a mechanical supply event rather than a fundamental catalyst. The merged entity also carries active reputational/regulatory exposure: a California AG cease-and-desist over Grok-generated deepfakes (Jan 2026), an ongoing federal CSAM class action against xAI, and a French prosecutors' investigation of X/xAI leadership, none of which has a hearing scheduled in the next ~90 days but all of which add real uncertainty. Between the lock-up supply overhang and the unresolved litigation/regulatory cloud, this doesn't clear the bar for a new long.
invalidation: Resolution of the CSAM litigation and regulatory probes without further escalation, an orderly pass through the remaining lock-up unlocks without disorderly selling, and a clear stock-specific (not sector) positive catalyst.
